notes.subject: Kowloon Development — Phase 3 Settlement Confirmed
notes.body: Met with Mr Lau at our Hong Kong office. He confirmed that the Phase 3 residential development settlement in Kowloon requires HKD 60 million by end of November 2026. This is a hard deadline — the developer has already issued the payment notice. Mr Lau asked us to review the portfolio liquidity position and consider options. He does not want to sell the core SHK Properties position if avoidable as he believes in the long-term recovery. Discussed using the existing Lombard facility to partially fund the requirement. He was receptive. I will prepare a liquidity waterfall analysis.

notes.subject: Portfolio Review — Concentration Discussion
notes.body: Mr Lau reviewed the portfolio. He noted the property concentration is intentional — he believes HK property is undervalued relative to long-term fundamentals. He is aware of the concentration risk. We discussed the structured product book (PF-0014B) — he noted the autocallable note (JB HK RE Basket) matures December 2026 and he expects it to autocall. He asked for an analysis of what happens if it does not autocall. I explained the mark-down and repayment at maturity. He understood. Re the Lombard: he is comfortable with current drawn level (~HKD 142m) but wants to know his headroom. I told him current LTV is ~49% against a 60% threshold. He was satisfied but I noted internally that the structured products facility (CF-0014-003) is much tighter — only 3.3% from threshold. Need to flag this.

notes.subject: China Housing Stimulus — Mr Lau Reaction
notes.body: Spoke with Mr Lau following the China housing stimulus announcement (June 18 2026). He was cautiously positive — noted that GBA policy relaxation for HK buyers in Shenzhen is interesting but his main focus remains HK Central/Kowloon Grade A. He does not plan to buy additional property at this stage given the upcoming November cash need.

notes.subject: Annual Review — Investment Objectives Confirmed
notes.body: Annual review conducted. Mr Lau confirmed investment objectives: capital preservation, maintain HK property exposure, generate income from bond holdings, and maintain flexibility for property development activities. He is not interested in broad diversification away from HK real estate at this time. Risk profile confirmed as Balanced. Mandate confirmed as Advisory. He expressed satisfaction with the RM relationship.

notes.subject: Diversification Portfolio Review — Hormuz Event Context
notes.body: Met with Mr Al-Mansoori and his family office CFO at our Dubai office. Discussion focused on the diversification portfolio (PF-0019B) performance and the impact of the Hormuz disruption on the core portfolio (PF-0019A). He acknowledged that the family's shipping and energy conglomerate was directly affected by the Hormuz event — vessel rerouting added significant cost in February-March. He wants the investment portfolio to provide a buffer against the operational business. He asked whether our current diversification strategy is sufficient. I noted the JB Shipping/Energy Note (INS-0024) is directly correlated with his operational exposure — this creates concentration, not diversification. He was surprised and asked for a detailed analysis. Also discussed the potential vessel acquisition — he said it is under board review and may require up to USD 50m capital, potentially by H1 2027.

notes.subject: Diversification Objective — Formal Statement
notes.body: Mr Al-Mansoori formally stated during the May 2026 review that the primary investment objective for the Julius Baer relationship is to provide DIVERSIFICATION from the family's core shipping and energy business concentration. He explicitly said: 'What we do in business, we should not also hold in this portfolio.' This statement should be recorded as a formal client objective. The family's wealth is approximately 65-70% concentrated in shipping/energy through the operating conglomerate (Al-Mansoori Group). He wants JB assets to move in a different direction.

notes.subject: Hormuz Disruption — Client Contact and Portfolio Response
notes.body: Contacted Mr Al-Mansoori during the Hormuz disruption (February 14-20 2026). He was in Dubai managing the operational business impact. He asked us to raise cash in the portfolio to demonstrate liquidity — we raised USD 4.1m in PF-0019A (confirmed transaction TXN-0005). The JB Shipping/Energy Structured Note declined to approximately 88 cents on the dollar. He noted this was problematic — 'I am losing money in my business AND in my portfolio from the same event.' This reinforced the diversification objective.

notes.subject: Inheritance Tax Settlement — Payment Schedule Confirmed
notes.body: Met with Frau Voss-Brenner in Munich. She confirmed the German inheritance tax settlement timeline with her German lawyer (Dr. Bauer). Two remaining instalments: EUR 4.2m due December 2026 and EUR 3.8m due June 2027. Total outstanding EUR 8m. She asked whether the portfolio can cover these without disruption to income. I noted that the EUR cash position (PF-0003A: EUR 4m + PF-0003B: EUR 2.5m) covers the first instalment but we need to think about the second. She does not want to sell bonds early. We should also note that the Conservative mandate means very limited equity exposure — she asked whether her 'Deutsche Bank shares are appropriate'. I noted that Deutsche Bank is a single stock representing ~15% of PF-0003A which seems elevated relative to the Conservative mandate guidelines. She said she inherited it and has sentimental attachment but acknowledged the concentration concern.

notes.subject: Portfolio Review — Mandate Alignment Check
notes.body: Quarterly portfolio review with Frau Voss-Brenner. Key issue: the JB Conservative Multi-Asset Fund (INS-0036) has increased its internal equity allocation following ECB rate cuts — the fund's factsheet now shows equity at 28%, above the fund's typical 20% target. Combined with the Deutsche Bank single stock holding (~15% of PF-0003A), total equity exposure in PF-0003A is approaching 36%. This exceeds the Conservative mandate equity ceiling of 30%. I flagged this to the client. She was concerned. I also noted that combined across PF-0003A and PF-0003B, total equity is approximately 28% — still above the Conservative mandate maximum of 30% on a combined basis if the MA fund equity proportion remains elevated. Recommend: (1) review MA fund equity allocation, (2) address Deutsche Bank concentration. Client asked for written analysis.

notes.subject: Annual Review — Client Objectives and Life Situation
notes.body: Annual review. Frau Voss-Brenner is 67 years old, widowed, living in Munich. Her two adult children (Michael and Anna) are named beneficiaries in her estate plan. She has no desire for capital growth — preservation of inheritance value and reliable income for living expenses are her sole objectives. She confirmed she does not wish to take on any additional risk. The German estate settlement has been emotionally stressful and she relies on the JB relationship for stability. She mentioned that both children have asked about their inheritance allocation — we should note succession planning as a medium-term topic.

notes.subject: Q3 Review — Swiss Property Interest
notes.body: Mr Whitfield considering Swiss property acquisition in Q4 2026 — approx CHF 5m deposit required. Portfolio has sufficient liquidity (CHF 10m MM fund) but want to pre-plan.

notes.subject: Energy Concentration + Capital Call
notes.body: Sorokina portfolio has significant Nvidia/Microsoft tech concentration alongside Gulf Energy Infrastructure exposure. Gulf Energy Fund capital call expected October 2026 (USD 5m). Client aware. Discussed Hormuz impact on Gulf Energy Fund marks. She was surprised by the indirect exposure. Portfolio has sufficient cash (CHF 15m) to cover the call.

notes.subject: Nvidia Concentration — Semiconductor Controls Risk
notes.body: Mr Cohen holds 74% in Nvidia (PF-0010). Discussed the August 20 2026 US semiconductor export control announcement. Nvidia fell 4% on the announcement. Cohen is aware — he says he has conviction but acknowledges the concentration. The margin facility (CF-0010-001) has USD 35m drawn. With Nvidia at current prices, LTV is comfortable at 25.4% vs 50% threshold. However a 50% fall in Nvidia from current levels would bring LTV to ~50% threshold — this is the margin call scenario.

notes.subject: Korea Semiconductor Export Controls — Portfolio Impact
notes.body: Called Mr Han immediately following the August 20 US semiconductor export control announcement. Samsung declined 8%, KOSPI semiconductor ETF -9%. His portfolio is ~50% in Korean semiconductor names. He was concerned but said he takes a long-term view. I noted the export controls specifically affect manufacturing equipment exports to China — Samsung's memory division has significant China revenues.
